messages:
aj: Heads up — proposing a change to the metrics label schema for token-level latency breakdowns and per-route KPIs. Goal: keep useful dimensions but avoid unbounded cardinality. Plan: introduce a versioned schema label, standardize seq_len buckets, limit kernel/model variant cardinality, and add cache flags (kv_hit).

maria: Can you sketch concrete labels? my main worry is model+kernel combos creating huge cardinality.

aj: Sure, example metric and label set:
```
metric: inference.token_latency_ms
labels: 
  route: string (logical route name, e.g. /chat/completions)
  model_id: short id (e.g. gpt-j-6b)
  model_version: semver-like string 
  kernel_family: one of {cpu_opt, cuda_sm80, cuda_sm90, triton} 
  kernel_version: whitelisted small set (v1,v2,...)
  quant: {fp16,int8,q4_0} 
  seq_len_bucket: {1-16,17-64,65-128,129-512,512+} 
  batch_size: {1,2,4,8,16,32+} 
  cache_state: {kv_hit, kv_miss} 
  deployment_tier: {hosted,dedicated,private} 
  schema_v: "v2"
```

kevin: Sequence buckets look fine. Are the batch_size buckets fixed too? do we need dynamic bucketing for spikes?

aj: Keep them fixed for ingestion efficiency. We can map observed sizes to the nearest bucket in the SDK before emitting. Dynamic buckets will blow up label cardinality.

neha: For route-level KPIs we also need rollups: per-route QPS, tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 token_latency. Those rollups should NOT include kernel_version or model_version to keep dashboards readable.

sam: How do we handle kernel_variant A/B experiments? kernel_variant name could be high-cardinality if we include hash suffixes.

aj: Good point. Strategy: record kernel_family + kernel_variant but restrict kernel_variant to a small enumerated set in metrics. For ad-hoc experiments, emit kernel_variant to logs only and a sampled metric (1% sample) with full variant for debugging. Production metrics must use the whitelisted variant names.

maria: What about labels coming from customer-provided data (e.g. route path params)? Must sanitize/normalize. Never include user_id, tenant_id, or long strings as labels.

aj: Agreed. Routes should be canonicalized to logical names (e.g. chat_completion) and not include path params. We'll add a sanitizer in the SDK and server-side ingress.

kevin: Telemetry cost question — do we enforce per-metric cardinality caps?

aj: Yes: enforcement plan: 1) schema_v label allows us to roll forward safely; 2) per-metric allowed-values whitelist in the metrics agent; 3) cardinality quota enforcement with dropped labels logged to an internal sink.

neha: Dashboards — we should version dashboards too and keep an alias map so old alerts keep working during migration. I'll own dashboard updates if you give me the final label list.

aj: Will do. Implementation plan: PR with label whitelist + seq_len mapping + SDK sanitizer, feature-flag rollout to staging (schema_v=v2), sampling knobs for kernel_variant. After 1 week of staging we flip in prod.

sam: Please open an issue with the migration steps and rollback plan so oncall can follow.

aj: Opened: https://redwood/infra/metrics/PR-432 — includes label lists, example Grafana panels to add: token-latency-by-route.p95, route-throughput, kv_cache_hit_rate, kernel-family-p95. Also added a note about updating alert detector rules.

deploy-bot: rollout started for metrics-agent v0.9.3 to staging :rocket:

maria: thumbs up. Once we see staging traffic, we'll check cardinality stats (top N label values) before prod flip.

aj: Thanks — I'll post a short follow-up with the exact whitelist JSON and sample ingestion dashboard tomorrow.

sam: Also add a retention note: high-cardinality debug metrics go to short-term hot store (7d) only.

aj: noted. :+1:
